root_cause_label: Incorrect task understanding and component selection due to SMILES misidentification and antibody target inference from purification tag
one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent misidentified the SMILES molecule as a folate analog (it is benzylguanine) and misread the His-tag at the end of the antibody heavy chain as the antibody's binding target, causing all five fusion protein components to be selected incorrectly without ever retrieving the actual task specification.
t_err_evidence: At step 6 the agent comments 'This appears to be a folate analog with pterin ring structure' for SMILES Nc3nc(OCc1ccccc1)c2nc[nH]c2n3, which is actually benzylguanine (a SNAP-tag substrate), establishing the false premise that drives all subsequent component selection errors.
t_commit_evidence: At step 13 the agent commits to its full implementation plan: 'antibody binder (His-tag) - donor (1H6R) - DHFR - acceptor (2H5Q) - molecule binder (3KZY)', specifying all five wrong components in the wrong identities; this plan is then executed without deviation through step 17.
trigger_explanation: The agent acted on two unverified wrong assumptions without checking: (1) it misidentified the SMILES Nc3nc(OCc1ccccc1)c2nc[nH]c2n3 as a folate analog when it is actually benzylguanine (a SNAP-tag substrate), and (2) it interpreted the C-terminal HHHHHHHH purification tag on the antibody heavy chain as meaning the antibody's target is a His-tag, rather than identifying the actual antibody target (FLAG peptide) through sequence-based search or metadata. These two false premises, combined with never reading the actual task specification, caused all five fusion protein components to be selected incorrectly.
forewarning_evidence: At step 9, the FPbase API query fails with 'Error querying FPbase: Expecting value: line 1 column 1 (char 0)' and returns zero donor/acceptor candidates, signaling that the agent cannot properly verify spectral properties of candidate fluorescent proteins. Despite this failure, the agent proceeds to select donor and acceptor by literature approximation rather than correcting the API query.
